definitions.gloss: wooden construction; timber-frame; made of wood
definitions.explanation: construction using wood as the primary structural material; used to describe buildings, houses, and other structures made primarily of timber

examples.japanese: この{家|いえ}は{木造|もくぞう}{二階建|にかいだ}てです。
examples.english: This house is a two-story wooden building.

examples.japanese: {木造|もくぞう}アパートは{家賃|やちん}が{安|やす}いことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Wooden apartments often have lower rent.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{伝統的|でんとうてき}な{建築|けんちく}は{木造|もくぞう}が{基本|きほん}だ。
examples.english: Traditional Japanese architecture is fundamentally wooden construction.

notes:
FORMATION:
{木|もく} (wood, tree) + {造|ぞう} (construction, making) → wooden construction

FUNCTIONS AS:
- Noun: {木造|もくぞう}の{建物|たてもの} (wooden building)
- No-adjective: {木造|もくぞう}{住宅|じゅうたく} (wooden house)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {木造|もくぞう}{住宅|じゅうたく} (wooden house)
- {木造|もくぞう}アパート (wooden apartment building)
- {木造|もくぞう}〜{階建|かいだ}て (wooden ~-story building)

CONSTRUCTION TYPES (used in real estate):
- {木造|もくぞう} (wooden)
- {鉄骨|てっこつ} (steel frame)
- {鉄筋|てっきん}コンクリート/RC (reinforced concrete)
- {鉄骨鉄筋|てっこつてっきん}コンクリート/SRC (steel-reinforced concrete)

HOUSING CONTEXT:
{木造|もくぞう} buildings are common in Japan and are generally less expensive than concrete structures. They are often considered to have better natural ventilation but may have less soundproofing.
